newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Six banks to compete for Costa Rica bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Six banks to compete for Costa Rica bond issue.

text.p: Six banks have been chosen to compete to place a $200 million bond from the government of Costa Rica, an official said on Tuesday.
The banks are Credit Swiss-First Boston, Chase Securities, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Lehman Brothers, JP Morgan and Salomon Brothers, deputy Finance Minister, Marvin Taylor, said.
A total of 19 banks put forward proposals to place the bond, he said, and the government will decide by July 31 which of the banks it will chose to lead the issue.
"The proposal is to have the funds available by the end of October or the start of November," he said.
Costa Rica plans to place about $500 million on international markets to help it cut its outstanding debt.
The placing of the remaining $300 million is seen for the first six months of 1998, officials have said.
Moody's Investors Service has given Costa Rica a Ba1 raing on its long-term foreign currency bonds.
